title: Al-Khaliq, the Creator
hookLine: the Creator, who makes from nothing

lines: READ, IN THE NAME OF YOUR LORD WHO CREATED.
cards: Before a tailor makes a single cut, the cloth lies on the table. The tailor measures, marks with chalk, measures again. Nothing is sewn yet, but in a way the coat already exists, in the measuring.
Classical Arabic dictionaries record a word for exactly that moment: khalaqa, to measure out leather or cloth before cutting it. It became the Qur'an's word for creating.

The verses tradition counts as the first revelation, the ones from camp four, use it twice in two lines: read, in the name of your Lord who created, created the human from a clinging clot. Today: Al-Khaliq, the Creator.

teach.b: The name opens the last verse of al-Hashr. Here is Pickthall: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. Three names in a row, and scholars, al-Ghazali among them, read them as three movements.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO MEASURES AND PLANS.
teach.b: Al-Khaliq, today: the one who determines, measures and plans what will be. Al-Bari', the Shaper out of naught: the one who brings it into being. Al-Musawwir, tomorrow's name: the one who gives it its form.
What makes the first more than a tailor? A tailor measures cloth that already exists. Muslim theologians teach that Allah creates from nothing at all: no cloth, no table, no chalk.
When He wills a thing, the Qur'an says, He only says to it, be, kun, and it is.

teach.h: KUN FA-YAKUN — BE, AND IT IS.
teach.b: Kun fa-yakun. And the Qur'an doesn't place creation only at the beginning. It speaks of Allah creating again and again: every birth, every morning, every seed that splits.
In this picture, a person didn't just happen once; they are held in being now. A curious detail: the Qur'an sometimes uses the same verb for people.
The prophet 'Isa, Jesus, says he shapes a bird from clay, by Allah's permission.
And after describing a child forming in the womb, it says, blessed is Allah, the best of creators. People make things too, measuring and shaping what's already there.
But making from nothing, and holding it in being, Muslim teaching gives to Allah alone.
In that view, everything in sight today was made.

how: Muslims affirm Allah as al-Khaliq, the Creator of everything from nothing, and reflect on creation as a sign; the name appears in names like Abdul-Khaliq, and the first revealed verses, read in the name of your Lord who created, are widely memorized.

o: the one who was himself made by another
the one who measures out and brings into being
the one who keeps the world in good order

games.q: three names, three movements — tap the pairs.

s: khalaqa once meant to measure leather before cutting
the word for measuring out became the word for creating.
the Qur'an never uses the verb create of anyone but Allah
'Isa shapes a bird from clay, and Allah is called the best of creators.
the Qur'an speaks of creation only at the beginning
it speaks of Allah creating again and again.

games.q: the first revelation begins: read, in the name of your Lord who… what?
games.why: who created, created the human from a clinging clot (96:1–2). in these first verses, the first thing said of the Lord is that He created.

practice: Take a sheet of paper, a napkin, a bit of string or a few leaves, and slowly make one small thing: fold a boat, tie a knot, arrange three stones.

Notice how much measuring happens first, your eyes planning, your fingers testing, then look at what you made and at the hands that made it, shaped long before you ever used them. If you pray, you can say, ya Khaliq, softly.

wordCard.voice: Al-Khaliq. The Creator, who measures out and brings into being from nothing, and who keeps creating. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Creator, from kh-l-q, first to measure out, then to create.

carryVoice: Your line: made. A cup, an apple, your own hand: in this view, all of it made. Day two hundred forty-two, done.

sources.q: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner.
